blocks.title: A namespace with a budget
blocks.what: A ResourceQuota works inside one namespace, so the file starts by creating quota-demo.
blocks.why: Teams often get a namespace each, with its own budget.
blocks.ifRemoved: The quota has no namespace to live in, so Kubernetes rejects it.
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: quota-demo

blocks.title: Add the ResourceQuota
blocks.what: Three dashes start a second object: a ResourceQuota, from the core v1 API.
blocks.why: A ResourceQuota caps the total that all Pods in its namespace can ask for.
blocks.ifRemoved: The file only creates the namespace.
blocks.comment: A second object: a ResourceQuota with a budget
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: quota-demo
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota

blocks.title: Name and namespace
blocks.what: This ResourceQuota is called team-budget and lives in quota-demo.
blocks.why: It counts every Pod created in quota-demo.
blocks.ifRemoved: Without the namespace, the budget lands in your current namespace, usually default.
blocks.comment: The quota’s name and the namespace it counts
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: quota-demo
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
metadata:
  name: team-budget
  namespace: quota-demo

blocks.title: A budget for requests
blocks.what: hard sets the totals. All Pods together may request 500m CPU and 256Mi memory.
blocks.why: Requests reserve room on nodes, so capping them shares the cluster fairly.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the quota, because it needs something to count.
blocks.comment: All Pods together may request at most this much
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: quota-demo
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
metadata:
  name: team-budget
  namespace: quota-demo
spec:
  hard:
    requests.cpu: 500m
    requests.memory: 256Mi

blocks.title: A budget for limits
blocks.what: All limits together may reach 1 CPU and 512Mi memory.
blocks.why: Every new container must now state its requests and limits, so the quota can count them.
blocks.ifRemoved: Limits are not counted, and containers need only state requests.
blocks.comment: All Pods together may set limits up to this much
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: quota-demo
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
metadata:
  name: team-budget
  namespace: quota-demo
spec:
  hard:
    requests.cpu: 500m
    requests.memory: 256Mi
    limits.cpu: "1"
    limits.memory: 512Mi

notes.---: Three dashes separate objects. One file can hold several objects.
notes.apiVersion: The API version. Namespaces and ResourceQuotas are both in the core v1 API.
notes.Namespace:kind: The type of object to create. A Namespace groups objects inside the cluster.
notes.ResourceQuota:kind: The type of object to create. A ResourceQuota caps a namespace’s totals.
notes.metadata: Details that identify the object, such as its name.
notes.Namespace:metadata.name: The Namespace’s name. It must be unique in the cluster.
notes.ResourceQuota:metadata.name: The quota’s name, used with kubectl describe resourcequota.
notes.metadata.namespace: The namespace whose Pods this quota counts.
notes.spec: The desired state: the totals the namespace may use.
notes.spec.hard: The totals. Kubernetes refuses any Pod that would take the namespace past them.
notes.spec.hard.requests.cpu: All CPU requests together may reach 500m, half a CPU core.
notes.spec.hard.requests.memory: All memory requests together may reach 256Mi.
notes.spec.hard.limits.cpu: All CPU limits together may reach 1 core. Quotes keep it a string.
notes.spec.hard.limits.memory: All memory limits together may reach 512Mi.

tryIt.result: Prints namespace/quota-demo created and resourcequota/team-budget created.
Refused: the quota needs every container to state its requests and limits.

expect: pods "no-sizes" is forbidden: failed quota: team-budget: must specify limits.cpu for: no-sizes; limits.memory for: no-sizes; requests.cpu for: no-sizes; requests.memory for: no-sizes

tryIt.result: The CPU and memory lesson’s Pod states its sizes, so it fits. Prints pod/sized-web created.
Used shows what sized-web takes from the budget, such as 250m of 500m requested CPU.
Deleting the namespace also deletes the quota and the sized-web Pod in it.

questions.question: A Pod in quota-demo sets no requests or limits. What happens?
questions.explain: When a quota counts CPU and memory, each container must state them. A LimitRange can fill them in.

questions.question: Two Pods each request 250m CPU. Can a third Pod requesting 250m start?
answers: Yes, there is no cap on Pods
No, it would take requests past 500m
questions.explain: The quota counts requests from every Pod together. 750m is more than the 500m allowed.

questions.question: How does a ResourceQuota differ from a LimitRange?
answers: A quota caps the namespace total. A LimitRange sets sizes for each container.
A quota covers one Pod only
questions.explain: They work well together. The LimitRange fills in sizes, and the quota adds them up.
